'''Sabacc game mode Dune Sea decks''' are draft sample decks for the Dune Sea table of the [[Sabacc game mode outline]]. They are one Light Side and one Dark Side deck, a ladder of Jawa dealers with their decks, and a boss deck for each side. A dealer deck with three extra Jawas gives the house an edge of about 2.3%.

''Status: planning and draft. Every card below is a real Decipher card; the decks are examples, not final lists.''

== How the decks are built ==

* '''Target.''' Each deck has the same 60-card spread as the standard fair deck, [[Sabacc game mode outline#Standard deck (decided)|Deck C]]. It holds 19 / 10 / 3 / 1 / 5 / 11 / 5 / 6 cards of value 0 to 7.
* '''Values.''' A card's value is the destiny number printed on it. Location cards have a destiny of zero.<ref name="ar2023">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook] (2023): destiny draws (PDF page 30) and Appendix C, Sabacc.</ref> The pages of virtual cards often show no destiny number, so only Decipher cards are used.
* '''Premise cards.''' Bill's starting premise is Jawas, sandcrawlers, Jawa weapons, and droids. Cards for these, and the locations named for Jawas, the Dune Sea, or sandcrawlers, are listed as ''premise cards''. Other Tatooine locations and Tatooine- or Dune Sea-flavoured creatures, vehicles, devices, and characters fill the remaining slots and are listed separately.
* '''Copies.''' The rulebook gives no copy limit that applies here. The drafts assume at most 3 copies of a card, and 2 of a unique (•) card.
* '''No sabacc Interrupt.''' [[Dune Sea Sabacc]] itself (value 5) is left out, as it starts the game.

== Cards available ==

Tatooine locations are the 0s: 26 Light Side and 22 Dark Side titles, counting the Tatooine systems and the sandcrawler sites. Premise cards other than locations are few and sit at 1 to 6. The only premise card worth 7 is the Dark Side [[Double Laser Cannon]], a sandcrawler weapon. The Light Side has none, and the other 7s that fit the theme are weak.

== Wild and clone cards ==

In [[Dune Sea Sabacc]] the wild cards (0–7) are sandcrawler sites, [[Magnetic Suction Tube]], [[Jawa Siesta]], and [[Jawa Pack]]. The clone cards are Tatooine locations, sandcrawlers, Jawa weapons, and [[Utinni!]].<ref name="dsabacc">[[Dune Sea Sabacc]] and [[Dune Sea Sabacc (Dark)]] game text.</ref> The Light Side draft above has 1 wild card and 21 clone cards; the Dark Side draft has 1 wild card and 23 clone cards. With the option button off, every card counts as its printed value and the odds below apply. With it on, more than a third of each deck becomes clone or wild, which changes the odds. That setting is not modelled.

== Too many Jawas ==

The Jawa cards are worth 2 or 3, and Deck C has only three 2s and one 3. A deck that follows Deck C exactly can hold about four Jawas. A deck with many Jawas needs a different spread. One draft uses a Jawa-heavy spread of 14 / 6 / 5 / 12 / 6 / 8 / 5 / 4. About half of each deck is premise cards (31 Light, 32 Dark). This spread moves the odds a lot:

{| class="wikitable"
! Player deck !! Dealer deck !! House edge !! Player win / push / loss %
|-
| Deck C || Deck C || −1.79% || 49.4 / 3.0 / 47.6
|-
| Jawa-heavy || Jawa-heavy || −3.07% || 49.7 / 3.7 / 46.6
|-
| Jawa-heavy || Deck C || −9.39% || 53.5 / 3.6 / 42.9
|-
| Deck C || Jawa-heavy || 8.43% || 43.4 / 3.7 / 53.0
|}

A player with Jawas and a dealer without them is far ahead; the reverse favours the house heavily. [[Jawa Ion Gun]] is worth 3, so it appears only in the [[#Jawa-heavy drafts|Jawa-heavy drafts]].

== Dealer's deck and the house edge ==

With the card game's rules (see [[Sabacc game mode outline#Going over 11 and ties (decided)|Going over 11 and ties]]) and the same deck on both sides, the player is ahead by 1.8% against a committed dealer. The dealer draws on 7 or less. Giving the dealer a different deck, shown openly, can restore a house edge of 2 to 2.5%. The player keeps Deck C.

{| class="wikitable"
! Dealer's deck !! Cards of value 0 to 7 !! Total !! House edge !! Player win / push / loss %
|-
| Deck C (no change) || 19, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 60 || −1.79% || 49.4 / 3.0 / 47.6
|-
| Add 2 zeros || 21, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 62 || −3.14% || 50.0 / 2.8 / 47.2
|-
| Add 4 zeros || 23, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 64 || −4.49% || 50.6 / 2.7 / 46.7
|-
| Remove 6 zeros || 13, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 54 || 2.17% || 47.8 / 3.3 / 48.9
|-
| Swap 2 zeros for 2 fives || 17, 10, 3, 1, 5, 13, 5, 6 || 60 || 1.93% || 47.7 / 3.2 / 49.1
|-
| Swap 2 zeros for 2 threes || 17, 10, 3, 3, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 60 || 1.08% || 47.8 / 3.2 / 48.9
|-
| '''Swap 3 zeros for 3 threes (Jawas)''' || 16, 10, 3, 4, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 60 || 2.34% || 47.2 / 3.3 / 49.5
|-
| Swap 3 ones for 3 threes || 19, 7, 3, 4, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 60 || 2.04% || 47.4 / 3.2 / 49.4
|-
| Swap 5 sevens for 5 zeros || 24, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 1 || 60 || 2.31% || 46.9 / 2.6 / 50.5
|}

The figures are exact, calculated with endless decks. The dealer draws on 7 or less and never looks at the player's hand. The player hits or stands as well as possible at every step. A perfect sabacc pays double both ways, a hand has six cards at most, and wild and clone cards are not modelled. An endless-deck simulation of 1,000,000 hands with the same strategy checked the Deck C row and the bold row. It agrees with the exact figures within its margin of error (about 0.1 points). One finite 60-card deck was not simulated for these decks. A negative edge means the player is ahead. Details are on the [[Talk:Sabacc game mode outline|talk page]].

Adding zeros to the dealer's deck does the opposite of what one might expect: the player gains. The edge comes from giving the dealer fewer zeros or more mid-sized cards. The bold row replaces three locations with three Jawas worth 3, which fits the theme and brings the house to about 2.3%. If equal card counts went to the dealer instead of a draw, the same deck would give the house about 5.4%. That tie rule would need a weaker dealer deck.

== Boss decks ==

'''R'kik D'nec (Light Side boss).''' [[R'kik D'nec, Hero Of The Dune Sea]] is a Jawa whose card says: "When he is playing Dune Sea Sabacc and wins, he wins double." His deck list is under [[#Boss deck lists|Boss deck lists]]. It has the 16 / 10 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 11 / 5 / 6 spread, a house edge of 2.34% before his card text. The text is a large number if read literally:

{| class="wikitable"
! How R'kik's double works !! House edge
|-
| No double (deck only) || 2.34%
|-
| 1 win in 20 doubles || 4.59%
|-
| 1 win in 10 doubles || 6.84%
|-
| 1 win in 4 doubles || 13.59%
|-
| Every win doubles (card text read literally) || 47.32%
|-
| Doubles only when he finishes on exactly 11 || 12.18%
|}

Each 1% of his wins that double adds about 0.45 points of house edge. A boss that doubles every win is practically unbeatable, so the double would have to be a rare, visible event or tied to the stake.

'''Iasa (Dark Side boss).''' [[Iasa, The Traitor Of Jawa Canyon]] has a Dune Sea Sabacc text close to Lando's: "When playing Dune Sea Sabacc, may subtract 1 from or add 1 to your total." His deck list is under [[#Boss deck lists|Boss deck lists]]. The table gives the house edge against Deck C if he may adjust on a share of hands. He moves his finished total one step toward 11, which is never worse for him. The numbers are therefore the same whether or not he sees the player's hand, as for Lando:

{| class="wikitable"
! Share of hands where he adjusts !! Deck C for both sides !! Dealer deck with three more Jawas
|-
| 0% || −1.79% || 2.34%
|-
| 5% || 0.27% || 4.36%
|-
| 10% || 2.33% || 6.38%
|-
| 25% || 8.51% || 12.42%
|-
| 50% || 18.78% || 22.47%
|-
| 100% || 39.19% || 42.46%
|}

== Contenders and decks (draft) ==

''Status: planning and draft, for Bill to review. The order of the ladder is a proposal and may be changed.''

Every Dune Sea dealer below is a unique Jawa character. The decks follow Bill's rules. They use real Decipher cards, at most 3 copies of a card (2 of a unique card), and the dealer's own card. Where the pool allows, one contender's cards are kept out of the other contenders' decks. The boss decks may use the earlier contenders' cards.

All the decks here use the dealer spread 16 / 10 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 11 / 5 / 6. Its three extra 3s replace three 0s of [[#Dealer's deck and the house edge|the dealer's deck above]]. Against a player on Deck C, the house edge is 2.34% (exact, endless deck). This assumes the card-game rules, a dealer who draws on 7 or less, and a perfect sabacc paying 2:1. A simulation of two separate 60-card decks, each reshuffled every hand, over 4,000,000 hands gave 2.39% ± 0.06. Every deck has the same spread, so every deck has the same base edge. The cards differ, and the bosses add a perk. Wild and clone cards are not modelled.

=== Level 1 decks ===

''Draft, revised after Bill's review on 12 October 2026 (see [[Talk:Sabacc game mode outline#Deck design principles (Bill)|deck design principles]]). Both decks use the dealer spread above, so the house edge against a Deck C player is 2.34%. Dathcha's deck mirrors Het Nkik's where a Dark Side match exists. Both are 60-card, one-side decks with locations to start from, so they could also be played as real decks (see the legality notes below).''

'''Light Side Level 1: Het Nkik. Theme: cheap and bad devices.''' Het Nkik is a very early, low-level contender, so most cards are deliberately bad. Most cards are from Premiere and A New Hope, with the Jedi Pack [[Han (Jedi Pack)|Han]] and [[Leia (Jedi Pack)|Leia]] and the Introductory Game [[Luke (Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game)|Luke]]. The 0s, the 1s, and most of the 5s and 6s are Bill's own picks. Cards from later sets tie to the deck's characters: [[Luke's Backpack]] (Dagobah) can carry Jawas, and Luke is in the deck. Neither Premiere nor A New Hope has a Light Side card worth 7.

Weak synergies kept on purpose:
* [[Don't Get Cocky]] with Han and Luke
* [[Leia's Sporting Blaster]] on Leia

* [[Luke's Backpack]] with Luke and Het Nkik

The rest is deliberately weak. R5-D4 is a "cheap astromech" with a blown motivator, and [[Remote]] is Luke's training remote. [[Bionic Hand]] needs a Disarmed character that the deck does not have.

Deploy paths: the Introductory Game Vader "must deploy on Death Star, but may move elsewhere", so the deck carries [[Death Star: Docking Bay 327 (Dark)|Death Star: Docking Bay 327]]. [[Vader's Obsession]] needs Vader to reach Luke on Tatooine, so the deck also carries [[Tatooine: Docking Bay 94 (Dark)|Docking Bay 94]], and Vader can use the docking bay transit between the two. They replace Bluffs and Mos Eisley in the 0s. The single Sandcrawler is worth 2, so [[R3-T6 (Arthree-Teesix)|R3-T6]] left the 2s to keep the spread. Both Vaders stay as the deck's few decent cards.

Weak synergies kept on purpose:
* the Dark Side Caller deploys on an Imperial or Jawa, so Dathcha can steal a droid held by a Restraining Bolt
* [[I Find Your Lack Of Faith Disturbing]] on Vader
* [[Charming To The Last]] with Tarkin (the mirror of Don't Get Cocky)
* [[Your Powers Are Weak, Old Man]] and Vader's Obsession with Vader
* [[Jawa Blaster]] on Dathcha
* [[Double Laser Cannon]] on the Sandcrawler
* [[Dune Sea Sabacc (Dark)|Dune Sea Sabacc]] needs a Jawa at a Tatooine site, so Dathcha can play the game this mode is built on
* [[Krayt Dragon]] with [[Tatooine: Krayt Dragon Pass|Krayt Dragon Pass]] and [[Krayt Dragon Bones]]
* [[Boring Conversation Anyway]] can cancel Het's Don't Get Cocky

The rest is deliberately weak junk from a trader's stock: [[Stormtrooper Backpack]] needs a trooper, [[Jawa Blaster]] can explode, and [[Ommni Box]] only shuffles a pile. Premiere and A New Hope have no Dark Side card worth 7, so the 7s come from later sets. [[Mournful Roar]] only works on a Chewbacca the opponent does not have, a deliberately dead card. [[Hunting Party]] is unique, so it is capped at 2 copies.

'''Legality notes.''' Each deck has exactly 60 cards, all from one side, with Tatooine sites to start from, and no objective. Every set used is a printed Decipher product, so the decks fit an open format. The Players Committee's Limited Resources format lists the Introductory Game and the Jedi Pack as "All Cards Legal". Because of the later-set cards, neither deck is legal in the Premiere - A New Hope format. The limit of 3 copies (2 of a unique card) is this project's own rule, stricter than the game. Decks for Campaign mode may later be cut to about 40 cards.

=== Boss deck lists ===

The two boss decks use the same spread, so each starts at the same 2.34% before the boss's perk.

'''Light Side boss: R'kik D'nec'''
R'kik is worth 1 and has 2 copies. His own 3s slot holds four of the five earlier contenders: [[Het Nkik]], [[Uutkik]], [[Thedit]], and [[Aved Luun]]. The 2s hold [[Kalit]] ×2 and [[Kalit's Sandcrawler]], so all five earlier Jawas appear. The 0s add [[Tatooine: Dune Sea]], the site of his lore, and the 5s and 6s use the strongest premise cards. The four 3s leave no room for [[Jawa Ion Gun]], which his text would deploy free; that would need one contender swapped out. The Virtual Set 8 version, [[R'kik D'nec, Hero Of The Dune Sea (V) (Virtual Set 8)]], has no Sabacc text, so the deck uses the Jabba's Palace card.

'''Dark Side boss: Iasa'''
Iasa is worth 1 and has 2 copies. The 2s hold [[Wittin]], [[Dathcha]], and [[Wittin's Sandcrawler]], and the 3s hold [[Daroe]], [[Nebit]], [[Herat]], and one [[Jawa (Dark)|Jawa]], so all five earlier Jawas appear. His own text takes 3 from the target's defense value when he fires a Jawa weapon, so [[Jawa Blaster]] ×2 is included. [[Tatooine: Jawa Canyon (Dark)|Jawa Canyon]] is in the 0s because of his title. '''Boss perks.''' Iasa's adjustment is modelled as the dealer moving his finished total one step toward 11 on a share of hands. Moving toward 11 is never worse for him, so the figure is the same whether or not he sees the player's hand. R'kik's double is modelled as a share of his wins that pay double. Proposal for a cap: one hand in ten for either boss, about 6.4% for Iasa and 6.8% for R'kik, against 2.34% for the contenders. One hand in twenty gives about 4.4% and 4.6%. The tables under [[#Boss decks|Boss decks]] have the full range.

=== Exclusive card pools (draft) ===

''Updated 12 October 2026 for the reworked Level 1 decks. Caller and Restraining Bolt moved from Uutkik to Het Nkik, and Luke's Backpack from Aved Luun to Het Nkik. The Dark Side Restraining Bolt moved from Daroe to Dathcha, and the Dark Side Sandcrawler from Nebit to Dathcha; Nebit gets Skiff instead. Ronto and Ronto (Dark) are reserved as a mirrored pair for a later Light Side and Dark Side contender matchup. The distinct-title and borrowed-card counts for contenders 2 to 5 predate the change and are marked –.'' ''A draft allocation, not built decks. It shows which cards each contender could keep for himself, and where the pool runs out.''

The hooks come from each contender's lore and text. The drafts for contenders 2 to 5 were built by an allocation program only to measure how much variety the pool gives; they are not proposed lists.

The 0s, 1s, 5s, and 7s run short; the 2s, 3s, 4s, and 6s do not. The 7s are the worst: each side has only 3 titles worth 7 with a Tatooine link, allowing 7 copies in all. The fourth title in each column is an artillery card with no Tatooine link. Only the 3s, with the Jawa characters, have room for real variety. Every contender can still have its own cards at 2, 3, 4, and 6, and the 0s differ by the location sets.

How the number of decks changes this (borrowed cards over all contender decks):

|-

|-
| 4 || 53 || 60
|-
| 5 || 97 || 108
|}

With 3 contender decks plus the boss, nothing but the 7s and a few 1s repeat. With 5, each of the later decks repeats roughly 20 to 30 cards, mostly 0s, 1s, 5s, and 7s. That is the trade-off for keeping all five Jawas.
